title_vi: Giao tiếp giữa các tiến trình trên Linux

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a git fetch of the pinned commit and hashed as a Git blob; computed OID matches the source map. Non-empty source was read; no source-image bytes used.

claims.evidence: pipe(7), mq_overview(7), signal(7), sem_overview(7) and shm_overview(7) of the Linux man-pages (clone at commit ae6b221, version 5.14) read; ping-pong of 100,000 round trips per mechanism measured with a small C program on a 4-vCPU KVM guest (Linux 6.18.44), signal coalescing and pipe capacity checked with Python.

mobile.evidence: Figure drawn by scripts/figures (viewBox width 320, smallest font 15 px, shown at 13.5 px at 320 px); python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser passed; the lesson (Markdown to HTML, optional sections open, 16 px side gutters) rendered in Chromium at 320, 375 and 430 px with no horizontal overflow of the page, any table or any code block. Not learner testing and not GitHub or a real phone.

claims.claim_vi: A pipe is a unidirectional channel with a read end and a write end; reading an empty pipe blocks and writing to a full pipe blocks; since Linux 2.6.11 the default capacity is 16 pages (65,536 bytes with 4,096-byte pages), which fcntl F_GETPIPE_SZ/F_SETPIPE_SZ can query and change, and the man page tells applications not to rely on a particular capacity; writes of at most PIPE_BUF bytes are atomic and PIPE_BUF is 4096 on Linux; a FIFO has a name in the filesystem and otherwise behaves like a pipe; writing to a pipe with no readers raises SIGPIPE.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mkerrisk/man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0 (man-pages 5.14). Capacity also read back with fcntl F_GETPIPE_SZ (65536) and PIPE_BUF with pathconf (4096) on the test machine.

claims.claim_vi: POSIX message queues deliver messages highest priority first; the limits msg_max and msgsize_max are set under /proc/sys/fs/mqueue (10 and 8192 on the test machine).
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mkerrisk/man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0; values read from /proc/sys/fs/mqueue on the test machine.

claims.claim_vi: SIGINT is generated by the keyboard interrupt and its default action is to terminate; a standard signal sent with kill carries no application data (sigqueue can attach one integer or pointer for a handler installed with SA_SIGINFO); standard signals do not queue: several instances generated while the signal is blocked are delivered once when unblocked (also tested: 5 SIGUSR1 sent while blocked ran the handler once, while 5 one-byte pipe writes were read back as 5 bytes).
claims.section: Standard signals; Queueing and delivery semantics for standard signals
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mkerrisk/man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0; coalescing tested in Python on the test machine on 2026-10-19. sigqueue(3) read at the same commit (man3/sigqueue.3).

claims.claim_vi: A POSIX semaphore is an integer never allowed to fall below zero; sem_post increments and sem_wait decrements, blocking while the value is zero.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mkerrisk/man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0.

claims.claim_vi: POSIX shared memory is created with shm_open, sized with ftruncate and mapped with mmap.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of mkerrisk/man-pages at commit ae6b221882ce71ba82fcdbe02419a225111502f0.

claims.claim_vi: Measured on one 4-vCPU KVM guest (Intel Xeon 2.1 GHz, Linux 6.18.44), 100,000 round trips of one byte, processes pinned to two cores (3 runs): pipes 24-27 us, Unix socket pair 26-33 us, POSIX message queue 24-27 us, shared memory with two semaphores 23-24 us, signals 25-26 us, shared memory polling a flag with sched_yield 0.3-0.4 us and polling without yielding 0.13-0.17 us; pinned to one core (4 runs): 2.7-3.2, 4.7-5.6, 2.7-3.2, 2.3-2.9, 2.9-3.9 us and, for polling with sched_yield, 1.5-2.2 us; polling without yielding on one core took about 8.1-8.2 ms per round trip (200 round trips, 3 runs), because the spinner keeps the core until the scheduler preempts it.
claims.verified_by: Experiment run by the author on 2026-10-19; C program with fork, sched_setaffinity, pipe, socketpair, mq_open, sem_init in MAP_SHARED memory, sigwait and an atomic flag; times taken with CLOCK_MONOTONIC. The two flag-polling rows were measured again with a separate C program (spin variants with and without sched_yield, 3 runs each) after review showed that the first harness called sched_yield in its wait loop.

claims.claim_vi: Five ways: pipe, message queue, signal, semaphore, shared memory.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung ghi chú: năm cách, và kết quả đo một vòng đi về. Hình không vẽ mũi tên giữa các tiến trình vì năm cách có hình dạng khác nhau và phép đo là điểm chính của bài.
source_deviations: Source describes a semaphore as a memory location tested and set by several processes; the lesson follows sem_overview(7): a non-negative integer with post and wait.
The lesson adds pipe capacity, PIPE_BUF, message priority, signal coalescing and an IPC latency measurement that the source does not contain.
